user_text: Plan a 1-day migration from SVN to Git for a small repo.
assistant_text:
# 1-Day SVN → Git Migration Plan

## Prerequisites (Night Before)
- [ ] Install `git-svn` or `svn2git`
- [ ] Collect all SVN committer usernames
- [ ] Notify team: SVN is **read-only** starting migration day

---

## Morning (2–3 hrs): Prep & Convert

### 1. Create Authors File (30 min)
```bash
# Extract SVN authors
svn log svn://your-repo --xml --quiet | \
  grep author | sort -u | \
  perl -pe 's/<author>(.*?)<\/author>/$1 = $1 <$1\@company.com>/' \
  > authors.txt
```
Edit `authors.txt`:
```
jsmith = John Smith <jsmith@company.com>
mjones = Mary Jones <mjones@company.com>
```

### 2. Run Migration (1–2 hrs)
```bash
# Standard SVN layout (trunk/branches/tags)
git svn clone svn://your-repo/project \
  --stdlayout \
  --authors-file=authors.txt \
  --no-metadata \
  -s my-repo

cd my-repo
```

### 3. Convert Tags & Branches (30 min)
```bash
# Convert SVN tags to Git tags
git for-each-ref refs/remotes/tags | cut -d / -f 5- | while read tag; do
  git tag "$tag" "refs/remotes/tags/$tag"
  git branch -r -d "tags/$tag"
done

# Convert SVN branches to Git branches
git for-each-ref refs/remotes | grep -v tags | cut -d / -f 4- | while read branch; do
  git checkout -b "$branch" "refs/remotes/$branch"
done
```

---

## Midday (1–2 hrs): Validate

| Check | Command |
|-------|---------|
| Commit count matches | `git log --oneline \| wc -l` |
| Branches present | `git branch -a` |
| Tags present | `git tag -l` |
| File diff | Compare random files SVN vs Git |
| History spot-check | `git log --oneline -20` |

---

## Afternoon (2–3 hrs): Push & Switch

### 1. Push to Remote
```bash
# Add remote (GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket)
git remote add origin git@github.com:org/my-repo.git
git push -u origin --all
git push origin --tags
```

### 2. Add Git Essentials
```bash
# Add .gitignore (convert from svn:ignore)
git svn show-ignore > .gitignore
git add .gitignore && git commit -m "Add .gitignore"
git push
```

### 3. Team Onboarding
```bash
# Each developer runs:
git clone git@github.com:org/my-repo.git
```

---

## End of Day: Cleanup
- [ ] Archive/lock SVN repo (set to read-only)
- [ ] Update CI/CD pipelines to point to Git
- [ ] Update any documentation/wikis
- [ ] Send team announcement with new repo URL

---

## Rollback Plan
> SVN repo stays **read-only** (not deleted) for 2 weeks as backup

---

**Tools:** `git-svn` (built-in) or [`svn2git`](https://github.com/nirvdrum/svn2git) for simpler syntax.

## Top 3 Migration Risks

### 1. 🧑‍💻 Author Mapping Incomplete
**Risk:** Commits with unmapped authors cause migration to **fail or show wrong names.**
**Mitigation:** Run author extraction against full SVN log before migration day; validate 100% coverage.

---

### 2. 📜 History Corruption / Loss
**Risk:** Mergeinfo, binary files, or non-standard SVN layouts cause **missing commits or broken history.**
**Mitigation:** Do a commit count comparison and spot-check file history on key files before cutting over.

---

### 3. ⏰ Migration Takes Longer Than Expected
**Risk:** Large history = slow `git svn clone` — can take **hours and stall the whole plan.**
**Mitigation:** Do a **trial run** the night before to get a realistic time estimate.

## Migration Checklist

**Before**
- [ ] Trial run completed
- [ ] Authors file 100% mapped
- [ ] Team notified, SVN frozen

**During**
- [ ] Commit count matches
- [ ] All branches/tags present
- [ ] Files spot-checked

**After**
- [ ] Pushed to remote
- [ ] CI/CD updated
- [ ] SVN archived (not deleted)
- [ ] Team cloned new repo
Keep the SVN repository **read-only but intact** for 2 weeks — if anything goes wrong, revert CI/CD and team access back to SVN immediately.
Install `git-svn` on the machine performing the migration.

user_text: What is the fastest validation step?
assistant_text:
Compare commit counts:

```bash
git log --oneline | wc -l
```
Match it against the SVN revision count — instant pass/fail.
**9am** Freeze SVN → **10am** Migrate → **12pm** Validate → **2pm** Push to Git → **3pm** Team onboards → **5pm** Done.

user_text: Provide two tools you might use.
assistant_text:
1. **`git-svn`** — built into Git, handles the core SVN-to-Git conversion.
2. **`svn2git`** — simpler wrapper that automates branch/tag cleanup automatically.

user_text: State who should approve the final cutover.
assistant_text: The **project or team lead** — they confirm validation passed and give the go-ahead to switch the team off SVN.
Send one clear message to the whole team **before and after** — include the new repo URL, cutover time, and who to contact if something breaks.

## Final Recap

- **Prep:** Freeze SVN, map authors, do a trial run
- **Migrate:** Use `git-svn` or `svn2git`
- **Validate:** Match commit counts, check branches/tags
- **Cutover:** Push to remote, update CI/CD, onboard team
- **Safety net:** Keep SVN read-only for 2 weeks
- **Approval:** Team lead signs off before cutover
- **Comms:** Notify team before and after with new repo URL

> Total time: 1 day. Biggest risk: incomplete author mapping.

- Freeze SVN early
- Map all authors first
- Trial run night before
- Use `git-svn` or `svn2git`
- Validate commit counts
- Team lead approves cutover
- Push to remote, update CI/CD
- Keep SVN as backup 2 weeks
- Notify team before and after
